seo.title: Case study: sneaker reseller stock and orders in sync · Coelor
seo.description: How a Dutch sneaker reseller keeps StockX, eBay and its Shopify store in sync with its warehouse: 31,000+ products matched, stock checked every 10 minutes, orders imported every 5.

hero.headline: One stock count across StockX, eBay and your webshop.
hero.sub: How a Dutch sneaker reseller stopped overselling and stopped retyping marketplace orders into its warehouse system.

problem.headline: Every pair lives in four places at once.
problem.body: The same pair is listed size by size on StockX, eBay and the webshop, while the real stock sits in the warehouse system. Every sale has to show up everywhere, fast.

items.title: Sold twice
items.body: A size sells on StockX and stays live on the webshop. The second buyer gets a cancellation, and the marketplace counts it against you.

items.title: Orders retyped
items.body: Marketplace orders are copied into the warehouse system by hand before anyone can pick and ship them.

items.title: Listings paused by hand
items.body: After each sale someone pauses the same product on the other channels, size by size.

items.title: Spreadsheets as glue
items.body: Stock exports downloaded, cleaned and re-uploaded, with thousands of product and size combinations to match.

setup.headline: The warehouse is the single source of truth.
setup.body: Coelor sits between the sales channels and the warehouse. It reads stock from the warehouse, pushes it to every channel and brings every order back.
before: Sold-out listings paused by hand after each sale
Marketplace orders retyped into the warehouse system
An item could sell twice before anyone noticed
after: Stock checked every 10 minutes on every channel
Orders imported every 5 minutes, warehouse order created
Every action logged; dry-run verified before go-live

steps.title: Match every product and size
steps.body: Each product is matched across the webshop, the marketplaces and the warehouse: more than 31,000 of them.

steps.title: Sync stock every 10 minutes
steps.body: Warehouse stock is checked every 10 minutes and pushed to every channel, so a sold size disappears everywhere.

steps.title: Import orders every 5 minutes
steps.body: Marketplace orders land in the warehouse system within 5 minutes as warehouse orders, ready to pick. No retyping.

steps.title: Log and verify every action
steps.body: Every action is logged. The setup ran in dry-run first, so the team saw each step before it went live.

fit.headline: Built for sneaker sellers who have outgrown manual work.
items: You sell on StockX, Alias, eBay or other marketplaces and on your own store
You keep stock per size in a warehouse or inventory system
You have hundreds or thousands of product and size combinations
Someone on your team pauses listings or retypes orders every day

offer.title: How we start
items: A 30-minute call to map your channels and stock flow
A written scope and a fixed quote
Most builds run in 3 to 6 weeks, in dry-run first

items.q: Do we have to change our webshop or warehouse system?
items.a: No. Coelor connects to the systems you already run through their APIs. If a system has no API, we work from its exports.
The build above connects Shopify, StockX and eBay to Picqer, Xero and Google Sheets. We also work with WooCommerce, Linnworks, Odoo and ChannelEngine, and can add other marketplaces that have an API.

items.q: What happens if a marketplace API goes down?
items.a: Runs retry and resume where they stopped. Nothing is applied twice. You get an alert if a run fails twice in a row.

items.q: Can we see what it will do before it changes anything?
items.a: Yes. Every automation runs in dry-run first and logs each action it would take, without taking it.
Most builds take 3 to 6 weeks from the first call, including the dry-run period next to your team.

contact.body: Which channels, which warehouse system, roughly how many products. We reply within one business day.
